items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Michel Hausser knocked on my door... asked me to come and help him talk to Dante... everyone of the group except Lily... was in Dante's room

ctx.x: Burnier had engaged for this tour Albert Nicholas, Don Byas (tenor) who was now living in Amsterdam, Holland and the trio of Michel Hausser which had Ricardo Galleazzi, an Argentinian bass player, who was also a fine trombone man, Dante Agostini, an Italian drummer, who was born in France and had never been to Italy before and on piano.
Michel Hausser was a real gifted vibraphone player and accordionist who was the best vibraphonist in France at that period and his style was formed on that of Milt Jackson.

Pope Pius XII had just died when we arrived in Milano and it was a bad beginning for the tour. We rehearsed at a place called the Arhetusa which was a bar and restaurant on the first floor and a club in the cellar. I had rehearsed and also sat in with the band of the Arhetusa before and the owner knew me quite well and called me "Maestro".
